claim: Expert parallelism's communication volume and all-to-all latency are O(k) in the number of activated experts, its traffic is load-imbalanced, and its routing-dependent communication requires an extra metadata exchange to stay deterministic.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP's communication cost grows with top-k and therefore scales badly on a slow fabric
scope_conditions: standard EP where each token is replicated k times and sent via all-to-all
quoted_support: EP has three limitations. First, both communication volume and all-to-all latency are O(k). Second, expert load imbalance further degrades all-to-all performance. Third, non-deterministic communication necessitates an additional all-to-all to exchange metadata.

claim: Head Parallel moves the inter-GPU transfer before any routing decision by splitting each token into Nh sub-tokens with independent routers, giving O(1) communication volume regardless of k, perfectly balanced traffic, and deterministic communication.
stance_target: the claim that MoE training on a slow fabric is necessarily communication-bound by top-k
scope_conditions: Multi-Head LatentMoE with Nh heads, P GPUs where P <= Nh; compatible with EP for scaling beyond Nh
quoted_support: The sub-tokens are distributed to GPUs before any routing decision. Each GPU completes all routing and expert computation locally. This has three advantages over EP: 1. Communication volume is constant because each token is sent exactly once before routing. 2. Traffic is balanced... 3. The inter-GPU communication is deterministic.

claim: Multi-Head LatentMoE with Head Parallel trains 1.11x faster at 2B total parameters (31.68 vs 35.36 hours) and 1.61x faster at 4B (34.41 vs 55.34 hours) than MoE with EP at comparable model quality.
stance_target: the claim that communication-efficient MoE architectures can recover much of the throughput lost to a slow fabric
scope_conditions: 10B-token FineWeb-EDU subset; H100 80GB NVLink; controlled compute budget
quoted_support: Multi-Head LatentMoE HP achieves comparable model performance to baselines while training significantly faster: 1.11x faster at 2B total parameters (31.68 vs 35.36 hours) and 1.61x faster at 4B total parameters (34.41 vs 55.34 hours).

claim: IO-aware routing performs online top-k directly in SRAM, reducing HBM access from O(T*Ne + Ne) to O(T + Ne) and avoiding the Nh-fold multiplication of HBM usage and IO cost that a naive Multi-Head LatentMoE implementation would incur.
stance_target: whether the architecture's memory advantage survives implementation
scope_conditions: Nh heads, T tokens, Ne experts; block-wise SRAM top-k
quoted_support: A naive implementation of Multi-Head LatentMoE would multiply High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) usage and IO cost by Nh... We develop IO-aware routing by doing online top-k directly in SRAM, reducing HBM access from O(T*Ne + Ne) to O(T + Ne).

claim: Head Parallel's expert computation is dropless and numerically correct like Grouped GEMM but implemented in pure PyTorch, so practitioners with a limited engineering budget can avoid writing custom CUDA kernels or adding new hardware support.
stance_target: the implementation cost of trying a fabric-friendly MoE architecture on an unusual GPU (sm_80 CMP 170HX)
scope_conditions: pure-PyTorch implementation using FlexAttention and torch.gather
quoted_support: The implementation is pure-PyTorch. Practitioners with a limited engineering budget can avoid writing custom CUDA kernels or expanding support for new hardwares.

claim: Using Head Parallel for inter-node traffic and EP for intra-node traffic is a possible direction for large-scale training, and HP on 8 to 16 GPUs is sufficient for most academic settings.
stance_target: how a fabric-constrained 5-GPU box could compose HP with EP
quoted_support: Experiments show that parallelism on 8 to 16 GPUs are sufficient for most academic settings, using HP for inter-node traffic and EP for intra-node traffic is a possible direction for large scale training.
